title: Grain-Boundary Scattering between Chiral Domains in Chiral Topological Semimetal CoSi
authors: Nicholas A. Lanzillo, Ion Garate, Ching-Tzu Chen
abstract: We evaluate the electron scattering properties in CoSi thin films having either twin (heterochiral) or non-twin (homochiral) grain boundaries using first-principles quantum transport calculations. We find that scattering across a twin grain boundary is more resistive than scattering across a non-twin grain boundary and that non-twin grain boundaries have a greater percentage of surface conduction than twin grain boundaries. This is corroborated by the transmission eigenstate profiles, which show that the surface Fermi-arc electrons can transmit past the non-twin grain boundaries between homochiral domains on the same surface without significant backscattering. In contrast, these surface electrons get scattered along the twin grain boundaries between heterochiral domains to the opposite surface, resulting in partial forward transmission and partial backscattering that yields higher grain-boundary resistivity. This work helps elucidate the complexities of electron transport in chiral topological semimetals for potential application in next-generation nano-interconnects.
summary: This work uses quantum transport calculations to compare electron scattering in CoSi thin films containing twin versus non-twin grain boundaries. The findings show that non-twin boundaries lead to lower resistivity and better surface conduction compared to twin boundaries. This suggests that controlling the grain boundary structure is crucial for developing CoSi for next-generation nano-interconnects.
main_problem: The study investigates how grain boundaries, specifically comparing twin (heterochiral) and non-twin (homochiral) types, affect electron scattering and transport in chiral topological semimetal CoSi thin films.
main_result: Scattering across twin grain boundaries is found to be more resistive than non-twin boundaries, and non-twin boundaries maintain a higher percentage of surface conduction, suggesting structural control can enhance electronic transport.
method: The research employs first-principles quantum transport calculations, utilizing Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Non-Equilibrium Green’s Functions (NEGF) to model electron transmission.
model_or_system: The physical system is CoSi thin films exhibiting chiral topological semimetal properties. The model compares transport across two types of grain boundaries: twin (heterochiral) and non-twin (homochiral).
key_observables: Specific resistivity (R_A), percentage of surface vs. bulk electron conduction, and momentum-resolved transmission eigenstates.
important_parameters: Film thickness (ranging from 2uc to 10uc), and the structural difference between twin and non-twin grain boundaries.
main_assumptions: The most energetically favorable lateral displacement (0.4x) found in bulk calculations is assumed to hold for thin films, and the analysis focuses on the symmetric (100) grain boundary orientation.
figures_summary: Figures show the unit cell and schematic grain boundaries, plot resistivity vs. thickness for both boundary types, and display $k$-resolved transmission spectra and transmission eigenstates illustrating surface conduction differences.
paper_structure: The paper systematically calculates and compares the electronic transport properties (resistivity, surface conduction) across non-twin versus twin grain boundaries using NEGF, analyzing how the structural chirality dictates scattering mechanisms.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the concept of engineered interfaces (grain boundaries) controlling electronic state transmission echoes principles used in designing quantum devices or understanding decoherence pathways in open quantum systems.
